title: The Wall Gallery
about: Paintings for a wall-mounted TV used as a picture frame: the greatest works of the Louvre, Versailles and the Nelson-Atkins, and the Romantic-era masters, chosen as the good, the true and the beautiful for a Christian family. No nudity, sensual subjects or horror; famous works left out are listed under left_out so they can be restored.
rights: US law only. Every work is a painting made before 1931 by a painter who died before 1956, so the painting is US public domain; a faithful photograph of a 2D public-domain work carries no new US copyright (Bridgeman v. Corel). Images are linked from Wikimedia Commons, never rehosted full size.

louvre.name: The Louvre
louvre.terms: collections.louvre.fr shows each painting at about 1,000-1,500 px and credits the photograph to GrandPalaisRmn. Its terms (art. 4.1.1.2) allow free use 'for any non-collective use within a strictly private context'; other uses need a written request to Rmn-GP.

versailles.name: Versailles
versailles.terms: The Palace's Digital Media Library is reserved for tourism professionals promoting Versailles; other use needs the Palace's agreement, and online use is capped at 1280x1024. The collections site (collections.chateauversailles.fr) shows small images and posts no reuse terms. Photographs are handled by RMN (photo@rmn.fr).

nelson-atkins.name: The Nelson-Atkins, Kansas City
nelson-atkins.terms: art.nelson-atkins.org offers a 'full' download of about 1,280 px. Its rights page says works may be under copyright, noted where possible, and leaves reuse beyond fair use to the user; larger images go through an Image Request Form.

romantic.name: The Romantic Age
romantic.terms: Held by many museums (Tate, the National Gallery, the Met, the Hermitage, the Tretyakov and others); each work lists its holder. Images are Wikimedia Commons photographs of the paintings.
